# `node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module`

**`process.getBuiltinModule()` to load a built-in module**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-node` (npm) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `version` |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (the call no longer goes through the module loader, which a bundler or a test mock may rely on) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-n/prefer-process-get-builtin-module` |

## What it checks

When every Node version the project supports has `process.getBuiltinModule()` (the `version` option or package.json's `engines.node` is within `^20.16.0 || >=22.3.0`), `require("<built-in>")` with the global `require` and `await import("<built-in>")` are reported. The suggestion rewrites the `require()`; an `import()` gives a namespace, so it is left to the author. With no Node range, or one reaching older versions, the rule does nothing, as upstream.

**Why:** `process.getBuiltinModule()` loads a built-in synchronously from either kind of module and can't pick up a package of the same name.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-node
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:node/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:node/recommended"]

[rules]
"node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | `string` | `""` | the Node versions the code runs on, as a semver range; by default package.json's engines.node |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module"]
severity = "error"

[rules."node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module".options]
version = ""
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = { severity = "error", options = { version = "<your value>" } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `version`

*string* · default `""`

the Node versions the code runs on, as a semver range; by default package.json's engines.node

```toml
[rules."node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module".options]
version = "<your value>"
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = { options = { version = "<your value>" } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module" = { severity = "warn", options = { version = "<your value>" } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"version": "<your value>"}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule node/prefer-process-get-builtin-module  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                          # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
// package.json
{ "name": "app", "engines": { "node": ">=22.3.0" } }
// src/a.js
const path = require("node:path");
```

#### Do

```js files
// package.json
{ "name": "app", "engines": { "node": ">=22.3.0" } }
// src/a.js
const path = process.getBuiltinModule("node:path");
```

#### Fixed

```js files
// package.json
{ "name": "app", "engines": { "node": ">=22.3.0" } }
// src/a.js
const path = process.getBuiltinModule("node:path");
```
